method: Web-browsed primary project documentation, versioned Rust API/source documentation, and upstream release/issue history. Sources are paraphrased in the index; no downloaded page or executable code is stored or run.

sources.title: Loro List and Movable List
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; JS/WASM examples; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Heading List and Movable List, lines 71-76 and 113-166.
sources.observed_operation: Shows List insert/delete, MovableList set/move, two replicas making concurrent moves and importing updates; both converge to one deterministic position, with the higher PeerID's move winning in the example.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: List is for insert/delete; simulating move with delete+insert can yield duplicate logical elements under concurrent edits. MovableList has native move/set but costs more; docs estimate about 80% slower encode/decode and 50% more memory for insert/delete-only workloads.
sources.applicability: Direct fit for ordered cue reordering; convergence does not present both move intents for human choice.

sources.title: Loro Cursor and Stable Positions
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: Separately storable cursor identifies a position in Text/List/MovableList; after insert/delete, it resolves to an updated position. Docs demonstrate cursors for comment ranges.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Integer indexes are unstable. When a referenced element is deleted, Loro recalculates the position by replaying relevant history and updates cursor metadata to refer to present elements; longer replay can cost more. JS offsets use UTF-16.
sources.applicability: Useful for optional text-range comments; cue-level comments should use an explicit cue_id rather than sequence indexes.

sources.title: Loro Sync
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Real-time Collaboration and Sync Strategies, lines 77-120; Import Status/Pending Operations, lines 184-200.
sources.observed_operation: Exports updates from a peer version vector and imports them; same state is reached for the same updates independent of order/duplicates. Import status exposes pending causal dependencies. Regular child containers independently created under one Map key can hide a value; docs recommend ensure_mergeable_* for shared logical keys.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Convergence assumes peers eventually receive the same update set. Non-empty pending ranges mean required dependencies are missing. Conflicting regular child containers under one map key do not both appear as values.
sources.applicability: Supports offline update exchange, durable outbox/relay design, schema initialization, and explicit missing-range recovery.

sources.title: Loro Rust LoroDoc API and source
sources.version_or_commit: Rust crate loro 1.16.2, exact version page; docs.rs latest resolved to 1.16.2 during research.
sources.locator: LoroDoc import/export, import_batch, try_get_movable_list, checkout/frontiers methods; matching implementation index at https://docs.rs/loro/1.16.2/src/loro/lib.rs.html#3339.
sources.observed_operation: Rust API imports/exports snapshots and incremental updates; import_batch accepts arbitrary order; ImportStatus reports pending dependencies; checkout reads a selected frontier; Rust wrapper exposes get_movable_list and recoverable try_get_movable_list.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Library does not implement a network protocol or local storage; caller owns those. Pending import is incomplete until dependencies arrive. Checkout detaches state; reattach/checkout_to_latest before ordinary editing.
sources.applicability: Native Rust fit for Rust/Slint; evidence does not prove UI integration, Windows packaging, or team-scale performance.

sources.title: Loro PeerID Management
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; Rust API warning corroborated by S04; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Quick Reference and Automatic/Manual assignment, lines 75-103; Rust API set_peer_id pitfall in S04.
sources.observed_operation: Default creates a random PeerID per LoroDoc instance/session, including when loading the same document again; operation identity is (PeerID, counter).
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Never reuse PeerID across concurrent writers; duplicate IDs can yield conflicting operation IDs and document corruption. Manual fixed IDs require strict single-writer ownership.
sources.applicability: Requires process/session identity policy and duplicate-writer/recovery tests; relay does not remove this invariant.

sources.title: Loro upstream package release history
sources.version_or_commit: Latest observed JS/WASM package release loro-crdt@1.16.4, released 2026-09-30, verified commit 45708d0; distinguish this from Rust crate loro 1.16.2 in S04.
sources.locator: Release block loro-crdt@1.16.4, lines 241-295; adjacent 1.16.2 block/commit lines 515-548.
sources.observed_operation: 1.16.4 makes applyDiff/revertTo all-or-nothing on errors, rejects invalid unknown-container operations without trapping, repairs revived movable-list children, and makes failed imports leave state unchanged; 1.16.2 reports compatibility for old JS tree snapshots after moves.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release notes concern JS/WASM package distribution and do not automatically prove identical version/fix status in separately versioned Rust crate. Old format and duplicate PeerID scenarios require explicit migration/replay tests.
sources.applicability: Real history for failure atomicity, format compatibility, and recovery; pin and verify the Rust dependency independently.

sources.title: Loro import lock-order issue and fix PR
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-04-23; reproducer used loro-crdt@1.11.1, @loro-extended/repo@6.0.0-beta.0 and adapter-webrtc@6.0.0-beta.0; linked PR #958 merged 2026-04-25 as commit 0977ad1. Report mentions main commit 7dfda879.
sources.locator: Issue #957 summary/repro, lines 138-177 and 208-239; PR #958 merged-status and summary, lines 130-173 and 251-264.
sources.observed_operation: A user report observed lock-order panics on imports under a connected Node/WebRTC adapter. Merged PR #958 changed len_ops() to read a cached op count instead of re-locking OpLog, kept the count synchronized through imports/rollback, and added regression coverage.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific WASM/Node/third-party WebRTC adapter and high multi-document/two-tab load, not a Rust-native defect claim or proof of a present bug.
sources.applicability: Justifies testing chosen adapter with concurrent import, reconnect, load, and failure paths rather than validating only core merges.

sources.title: Automerge conflict behavior
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs; JS-oriented example, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: Concurrent assignments to one property yield a deterministic displayed winner and retained alternatives accessible through getConflicts; a later assignment clears the conflict.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Winner ordering uses operation IDs rather than wall-clock time. Alternatives stay inspectable only until code assigns the property again.
sources.applicability: Credible local-first/Rust alternative; UI must inspect/persist conflicts before overwriting and cannot treat LWW as approval.

sources.title: Automerge Lists
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs; JS examples; no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: Docs recommend updating list IDs and entity-map entries directly rather than replacing an entire nested object, because whole-object replacement conflicts at the containing property.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fine-grained edits help disjoint concurrent operations merge; they do not define a first-class move or stage-staff decision workflow.
sources.applicability: Relevant to cue ID list plus entity map if Automerge is chosen.

sources.title: Automerge Rust sync protocol
sources.version_or_commit: Official Rust API docs, generated version not exposed in captured page; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: Each synchronizing peer keeps per-peer sync state and exchanges generated/received messages in a loop.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Protocol assumes a reliable in-order stream between peers.
sources.applicability: Transport/relay must satisfy or wrap that stream contract.

sources.title: Yjs Offline Support
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs; y-indexeddb package path, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: y-indexeddb writes changes to local IndexedDB and loads them on the next visit; only latest updates are sent to the network provider; multiple providers can be combined.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Examples target browser IndexedDB; native applications need an environment-appropriate database provider from the ecosystem. Browser page assets need separate offline availability.
sources.applicability: Good web/JS alternative; adds provider/binding work for a Rust desktop UI.

sources.title: Yjs Relative Positions
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: A relative position attaches to an element, remains stable under remote insertion, can be encoded, and translates to a current index; resolution returns null if target type is deleted or unavailable.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to text/sequences in the same Yjs document; it does not establish cue-level identity.
sources.applicability: Strong alternate for text-span comments; stable cue IDs remain preferable for whole-cue anchors.

sources.title: ShareDB Introduction
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: ShareDB is a Node.js server/client for JSON collaboration; it delegates OT transformation to types and advertises offline change sync upon reconnection and historic versions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Server coordinates/commits; OT semantics depend on registered type plugin.
sources.applicability: Server-authoritative alternative with additional service and app policy needs.

sources.title: ShareDB Reconnecting Client Example
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.observed_operation: Reconnects with reconnecting-websocket but sets maxEnqueuedMessages=0 because ShareDB says buffering while the socket is closed has undefined behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Example disables WebSocket buffering and shows server-backed subscribe/submitOp; it is not a durable local outbox implementation.
sources.applicability: Requires separate durable client outbox/replay and server persistence for disconnected rehearsal work.
